title: Expand ticket engine to include epic lifecycle support
objective: Expand the Little Mester ticket engine to support full epic lifecycle management: epic grouping through the existing is_epic flag, child ticket relationship traversal, composite status computation, circular reference detection, and CLI/MCP tooling for epic queries.

acceptance_criteria.text: Epic grouping uses the existing `is_epic: true` flag on regular tickets; no new `type` value is added, preserving the 6-value enum in docs/DECISIONS.md D.2 and architecture/DECISIONS.md C.1.
Engine.getChildren(epicNumber) returns all tickets with parent=epicNumber, sorted by updated_at desc
Engine.getEpicStatus(epicNumber) computes composite status: 'resolved' only when ALL children are 'resolved' or 'archived'; 'active' when any child is 'active'; otherwise 'draft'
Engine.update() rejects parent assignments that would create circular references (A→B→C→A)
Engine.create() validates that a parent ticket exists before linking; returns error for non-existent parent
CLI gains 'list-children <epic-number>' command that prints children with their status and titles
CLI gains 'epic-status <epic-number>' command that prints composite status + breakdown per child
MCP server exposes listChildren(ticket_dir, epic_number) and getEpicStatus(ticket_dir, epic_number) tools
Index gains 'next_number' field for deterministic ID allocation under concurrent writes (per engine-plan D.10)
validate() checks that no ticket has a parent pointing to a non-existent ticket number

needed: unit tests for getChildren and getEpicStatus engine methods
CLI list-children and epic-status command tests
MCP tool integration tests for epic queries
end-to-end: create epic, add children, verify composite status
is_epic flag round-trips; type "epic" is rejected with a clear error

comments.author: cli
comments.body: Design reference: engine-plan.md section D.2 already documents epics as 'real tickets with lifecycle'. This ticket converts those design decisions into actual implementation. Key design points to implement: composite status auto-computed on read (not persisted), epics independently queryable, children depend upon parent. See docs/tickets/archive/engine-plan-v1-2026-10-25.md §D.2.

comments.author: cli
comments.body: RECONCILED 2026-10-26: A1 originally proposed adding "epic" as a seventh type. That conflicts with docs/DECISIONS.md D.2 (6-value type enum) and architecture/DECISIONS.md C.1 (epics are regular tickets flagged `is_epic: true`, with composite status computed on read). A1 now matches the documented design: no new type value, the engine must reject `type: "epic"` and rely on `is_epic`. This ticket enables the hierarchy used by epic #35 but is not part of its completion criteria.
